authors: C. Gnendiger, A. Signer, D. Stoeckinger, A. Broggio, A.L. Cherchiglia, F. Driencourt-Mangin, A.R. Fazio, B. Hiller, P. Mastrolia, T. Peraro, R. Pittau, G.M. Pruna, G. Rodrigo, M. Sampaio, G. Sborlini, W.J. Torres Bobadilla, F. Tramontano, Y. Ulrich, A. Visconti
title: To d, or not to d: recent developments and comparisons of regularization schemes
claim: Review and comparison of CDR, HV, FDH, DRED (Sec. 2), FDF/SDF (Sec. 3), IREG (Sec. 4), FDR (Sec. 5), FDU (Sec. 6) on simple NLO examples. Sec. 2.1 defines the schemes via the quasi-4-dimensional space QS[4] (QS[d] + QS[n_eps], n_eps = 2 eps), with strictly 4-dimensional S[4] as a subspace, and singular vs regular vector fields (Table 1); epsilon-scalars and evanescent couplings must be separated at multi-loop level in non-SUSY theories (eqs. 2.7-2.8; Sec. 2.2: up to (l-1) loops in an l-loop calculation, two-loop counterterm eq. 2.12). Sec. 2.4: Stoeckinger's construction removes Siegel's inconsistency; equivalence of FDH/DRED with CDR (Jack et al.) establishes unitarity/causality indirectly; for SUSY, DRED/FDH have significant advantages since in many cases SUSY is manifestly preserved, though no all-order proof exists; all-order statements for CDR/HV (BPHZ equivalence, QAP) hold in chiral theories only with non-anticommuting gamma5.
scheme: CDR, HV, FDH, DRED, FDF, SDF, IREG, FDR, FDU.
symmetry_argument: Review-level statements; SUSY: 'manifestly preserved in many cases' without all-order proof (Sec. 2.4).
